extracted.intended_audience: Small business applicants (biotech/antimicrobial) preparing SBIR/STTR Fast-Track grant applications and associated budgets/commercialization plans
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural content for preparing the commercialization plan, budget justification, SBIR/STTR eligibility questions, and go/no-go criteria for a Fast-Track antimicrobial development project (Phase I/II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use FDA guidance for ABSSSI development
rubrics_metrics.description: The FDA had published extensive Guidance for Industry on Developing Drugs for Treatment for Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections and we will use these guidelines throughout our development program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FDA guidance documents as the regulatory framework for preclinical and clinical development decisions and study design; use them to shape the overall development program and prepare for regulatory interactions (e.g., pre-IND).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance-rate go/no-go threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, a resistance rate higher than 10^-8 is considered too high to enter development for an antimicrobial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed frequency of resistance (e.g., from hollow-fiber or other models) as a quantitative go/no-go metric; do not proceed to Phase 2 unless resistance frequency for the combined therapeutic is acceptably below this threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I go/no-go based on hollow-fiber resistance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: In Phase I of this project, we will identify the best ADEP partnering antibiotic and we will evaluate the combinations for the potential to develop resistance in the hollow-fiber model. The frequency of resistance development will be the go-no-go decision point for this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform combination testing in hollow-fiber systems to measure resistance emergence; postpone Phase II until conclusive, acceptable resistance data are obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select animal models predictive of human outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: In Phase 2, the combination will be tested in animal models of MRSA infection, which are largely predictive of outcomes in humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose preclinical models known to correlate with human outcomes; prefer models in which standard front-line therapies fail so the new therapeutic can demonstrate clear superiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose models where standard therapies fail to show effect
rubrics_metrics.description: We have purposefully chosen models in which standard front-line therapies fail, allowing our therapeutic combination to demonstrate clear superiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design efficacy studies to highlight meaningful advantage over existing therapies by using challenging infection models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination therapy expectation for resistance suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Because an infection may contain more than 10^8 cells, rifampicin is not used alone for the treatment of S. aureus, but only in combination with another agent. In S. aureus, spontaneous resistance mutants arise at a frequency of around 10^-8 for selections with rifampicin or fusidic acids, but are undetectable (frequency <10^-11) for a combined treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for combination regimens that reduce observable resistance frequency substantially (ideally below detection limits, e.g., <10^-11) to justify development; use combination theory when interpreting mutation-frequency data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization plan content: value, outcomes, impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercialization Plan: Value of the SBIR Project, Expected Outcomes, and Impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the commercial value proposition, expected product outcomes, and the public health/commercial impact in the commercialization plan; for Phase II or Fast-Track include a full commercialization plan per agency-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2 objective: enable pre-IND meeting with FDA
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 2 constitutes a series of standard preclinical development studies, which will enable a pre-IND meeting with the FDA upon this project’s completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design Phase 2 studies to generate the data package necessary for regulatory engagement (pre-IND), including GLP/nonclinical studies as required by FDA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR eligibility certification at time of award
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you certify that at the time of award your organization will meet the eligibility criteria for a small business as defined in the funding opportunity announcement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must certify small-business status at award; consult FOA/agency-specific eligibility rules and complete the SBIR/STTR information questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of subcontracts with federal laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this application include subcontracts with Federal laboratories or any other Federal Government agencies? If yes, insert the names of the Federal laboratories/agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully disclose any federal lab/agency subcontracting in the application attachments as required by the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUBZone status disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you located in a HUBZone? To find out if your business is in a HUBZone, use the mapping utility provided by the Small Business Administration at its web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide HUBZone status as requested; use SBA tools to verify and include explanation/attachments if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan required for Phase II / Fast-Track
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are submitting a Phase II or Phase I/Phase II Fast-Track Application, include a Commercialization Plan in accordance with the agency announcement and/or agency-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a commercialization plan per agency format; failure to include required commercialization materials may render the application non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR PI employment and effort requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Question: Will the Project Director/Principal Investigator have his/her primary employment with the small business at the time of award? For STTR: (1) Does the Project Director/Principal Investigator have a formal appointment or commitment either with the small business directly (as an employee or a contractor) OR as an employee of the Research Institution ... AND (2) Will the Project Director/Principal Investigator devote at least 10% effort to the proposed project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the PI employment/effort questions accurately according to whether applying SBIR or STTR; for STTR the PI must have a formal appointment and devote ≥10% effort; for SBIR PI primary employment with small business at award is queried.

rubrics_metrics.name: STTR allocation of work percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: In the joint research and development proposed in this project, does the small business perform at least 40% of the work and the research institution named in the application perform at least 30% of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For STTR applications ensure the small business and research institution perform the minimum required percentages of R&D (small business ≥40%, research institution ≥30%) and document this in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Permission Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If this application does not result in an award, is the Government permitted to disclose the title of your proposed project, and the name, address, telephone number and e-mail address of the official signing for the applicant organization, to organizations that may be interested in contacting you for further information?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to the disclosure permission checkbox and provide any requested attachments if opting out or providing explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget structure and required sections (Research & Related Budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH & RELATED Budget sections A-K: includes Senior/Key Person (A), Other Personnel (B), Equipment (C), Travel (D), Participant/Trainee Support Costs (E), Other Direct Costs (F), Direct Costs totals (G), Indirect Costs (H), Total Direct and Indirect Costs (I), Fee (J), Budget Justification (K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate all budget sections A–K as applicable and attach a budget justification file explaining personnel effort, materials/supplies, consultant services, subawards, facilities rental, alterations, and other direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment reporting threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: List items and dollar amount for each item exceeding $5,000 (Equipment Description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include individual equipment line items >$5,000 with costs; attach additional equipment files where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant/Trainee support cost breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant/Trainee Support Costs must list Tuition/Fees/Health Insurance, Stipends, Travel, Subsistence, Other, and Number of Participants/Trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a line-item breakdown for participant support and include totals in Section E of the Research & Related budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect Cost Rate (%) and Indirect Cost Base ($) and identify Cognizant Federal Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report institutional F&A (indirect) rates, bases, and cognizant federal agency information; ensure consistency with institution's negotiated rate agreement (example in text: Arietis requesting F&A costs at 40% and fringe benefits at 35%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Justification should describe personnel roles and percent effort, materials and supplies estimates (~$20,000 per FTE/year), specific costs (e.g., $107,000 for ADEP4 synthesis), animal study costs per year ($44,000/year Y2-4), consultant hours and roles, travel and publication costs, and any fees (example: Arietis requests a fee of 7%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, itemized justification for requested funds, tie budget lines to project tasks, specify consultant roles/hours, CRO arrangements, and any one-time synthesis or outsourced study costs; include institutional overhead/fringe rates and requested fee percentage if allowed by agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative budget and totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cumulative budget view including totals for Sections A (Senior/Key Person), C (Equipment), D (Travel), E (Participant/Trainee), F (Other Direct Costs), G (Direct Costs), H (Indirect Costs), I (Total Direct and Indirect Costs), and J (Fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cumulative totals and summary pages as part of the Research & Related budget to present multi-year costs clearly.
